title: Responsive Design & Accessibility Checklist ♿
description: Ensure your pages work everywhere and for everyone.

slides.title: Responsive Design Checklist ✅
slides.content:
# Before You Ship

- ✅ Viewport meta tag present.
- ✅ Content readable without horizontal scroll at all widths.
- ✅ Touch targets at least 44×44px.
- ✅ Images use `srcset`/`<picture>` for resolution switching.
- ✅ No fixed widths that break; use `max-width`, `%`, `fr`, `auto`.
- ✅ Test on real devices or DevTools device mode.
- ✅ Typography scales fluidly (use `clamp()` or relative units).
- ✅ Navigation adapts to mobile (hamburger, off‑canvas, or priority+).

slides.title: Accessibility (A11y) Checklist ♿
slides.content:
# Inclusive Design

- ✅ Semantic HTML used (landmarks, headings in order).
- ✅ All images have meaningful `alt` text (or empty for decorative).
- ✅ Forms have labels; errors are communicated with text, not just colour.
- ✅ Focus styles are visible; `outline` not removed without replacement.
- ✅ Colour contrast meets WCAG AA.
- ✅ Page is fully keyboard navigable.
- ✅ `aria-*` attributes used only when HTML semantics aren't enough.
- ✅ `prefers-reduced-motion` respected.
- ✅ A 'skip to main content' link provided.

slides.title: Skip Link Implementation

quizData.question: If you use semantic HTML, you automatically meet all accessibility requirements.
quizData.explanation: Semantics help a lot, but you still need to handle colour contrast, focus indicators, alt text, keyboard traps, etc.

slides.title: Testing Tools 🧪
slides.content:
# Validate Your Work

- **Lighthouse** (Chrome DevTools) – audits performance, accessibility, SEO.
- **axe DevTools** – browser extension for accessibility issues.
- **WAVE** – visual feedback on accessibility.
- **HTML Validator** (validator.w3.org) – checks syntax.
- **CSS Validator** (jigsaw.w3.org) – checks CSS errors.

Run these before every project submission.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Test with a Screen Reader

Try navigating your page with VoiceOver (Mac) or NVDA (Windows). It's eye‑opening and reveals real‑world usability issues.
